key_insight: This paper shows that multimodal LLMs can be made faster by jointly adapting how much they look at the input and how much they think during inference. Instead of optimizing visual tokens or model computation separately, the method coordinates both to cut cost while preserving performance.
problem_solved: It addresses the high inference cost of multimodal large language models, caused by processing too many visual tokens and running a heavy LLM over them. Prior approaches usually reduce only one side of the problem, which limits efficiency gains.
method: Jointly adapt visual token usage and LLM compute during inference rather than treating them independently.
Identify and remove redundant visual information while also skipping unnecessary internal computation in the language model.
Balance token reduction and compute reduction to maintain accuracy while lowering latency and resource use.
impact: This matters because it makes multimodal AI systems more practical for real-world deployment on constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. For practitioners, it offers a path to faster and cheaper vision-language inference without sacrificing much quality.
visual_elements: Before-and-after pipeline diagram showing fewer visual tokens and fewer active LLM layers/heads.
Split bar chart comparing inference cost: baseline vs token-only pruning vs compute-only skipping vs joint adaptation.
Icon set illustrating an eye for visual tokens, a lightning bolt for compute, and a speedometer for latency.
Trade-off curve showing accuracy versus inference cost with the joint method in the favorable region.
paper_title: Look Less, Think Faster: Joint Token-Compute Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
paper_authors: Pengcheng Wang, Zhiquan Wang, Jayoung Lee, Zhuoyan Xu, Ran Xu
